facts.fact_text: The opposition planned to hold a demonstration on 17 November 2012 in Baku.
The opposition planned to hold a demonstration on 26 January 2013 in Baku.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 26 January 2013.
The Baku City Executive Authority refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
Shortly after the demonstration of 17 November 2012 had begun, the police started to disperse it.
Shortly after the demonstration of 26 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse it.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 26 January 2013.
In the first case (17 November 2012), the Sabail District Court found that the applicant had participated in an unauthorised demonstration.
In the second case (26 January 2013), the Sabail District Court found that the applicant had participated in an unauthorised demonstration.
By a decision of 17 November 2012, the Sabail District Court convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
By a decision of 17 November 2012, the Sabail District Court sentenced the applicant to five days' administrative detention.
By a decision of 26 January 2013, the Sabail District Court convicted the applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
By a decision of 26 January 2013, the Sabail District Court sentenced the applicant to a fine of 500 Azerbaijani manats (AZN).

The administrative-offence report issued on 17 November 2012 stated that by deliberately failing to comply with a lawful order from the police, the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

In the second case (26 January 2013), the applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences, which concerns participation in a public assembly that had not been organised in accordance with the law.
At the time of both of the applicant's arrests, under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 17 November 2012, Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that any breach of the rules, set forth under the legislation, on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets shall be punishable by a reprimand or a fine of seven to thirteen Azerbaijani manats.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 17 November 2012, Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that deliberate failure by an individual to comply with a lawful order of a police officer or military serviceman carrying out their duties to protect public order shall be punishable by a fine of twenty to twenty-five Azerbaijani manats or, if that sanction is inadequate in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the character of the offender, by administrative detention for a term of up to fifteen days.
The Baku City Executive Authority stated in general terms that the demonstration of 17 November 2012 was not in accordance with the Law on Freedom of Assembly.
The Baku City Executive Authority stated that the square where the organisers proposed to hold the assembly of 17 November 2012 was a designated public leisure area.
The Baku City Executive Authority stated that the assembly of 17 November 2012 was impractical.

According to the applicant, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The participants in the demonstration of 17 November 2012 were demanding democratic reforms in Azerbaijan.
The participants in the demonstration of 17 November 2012 were protesting against impediments to freedom of assembly.
The participants in the demonstration of 26 January 2013 were condemning the use of force by the police against participants of previous demonstrations.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, titled 'The honouring of obligations and commitments by Azerbaijan', stated that there is no political dialogue with the opposition parties outside parliament in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about the restrictive climate for the activities of the extra-parliamentary opposition in Azerbaijan, which complains about limitations imposed on freedom of expression and freedom of assembly and the lack of access to the public media.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that the establishment of an inclusive political system and a truly competitive and unrestrictive political environment in Azerbaijan requires full implementation of basic freedoms, including freedom of expression, freedom of assembly and freedom of association.
Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed deep concern about the situation regarding basic freedoms in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe raised concern about recently adopted amendments to the Criminal Code and the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan, which increased penalties for the organisers of, and participants in, 'unauthorised' gatherings.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that, considering the Azerbaijani authorities' ongoing blanket ban on protests in the Baku city centre, the amendments increasing penalties for organisers of and participants in unauthorised gatherings are likely to have a further negative impact on freedom of assembly and freedom of expression.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about the restrictive use of certain articles of the Criminal Code of Azerbaijan, in particular Articles 221 and 233, against participants in peaceful, albeit unauthorised, demonstrations.
The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 was authored by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks stated that the Commissioner is deeply concerned by the recent amendments to the Law on Freedom of Assembly, the Criminal Code and the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan, which further erode the right to freedom of assembly.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks stated that the sanctions which can now be imposed, coupled with the fact that local authorities have not authorised a single rally in Baku city centre in recent years, clearly have a chilling effect on the organisation of or participation in demonstrations in Azerbaijan.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks stated that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks urged the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that no disproportionate sanction, which would undermine the fundamental right to peaceful assembly, is imposed.
